references.text: Concerns the tithing laws mentioned in Deuteronomy 12:6, where the tithe of all from the land belongs to the Lord.
Describes how the Levites were to receive the tithe from the children of Israel, which is part of the offerings mentioned in the main verse.
Elaborates on the tithing laws and how they were to be brought to the place the Lord chose, directly parallel to Deuteronomy 12:6.
Deals with the firstborn of cattle and sheep that were to be consecrated to the Lord, as mentioned in the main verse.
Establishes the law that all firstborn belong to the Lord, which is the basis for the offering of the firstborn mentioned in the main verse.
Commands that the firstborn of sons and livestock be given to the Lord, parallel to the mention of the firstborn in the main verse.
Describes vow offerings and voluntary offerings that were to be eaten on the same day, corresponding to the vow offerings and voluntary gifts in the main verse.
Mentions burnt offerings and slaughter offerings as vow offerings or voluntary offerings, the same categories as in the main verse.
Concerns vows to the Lord and the importance of keeping them, directly linked to the vow offerings mentioned in the main verse.
Explains how Christ's sacrifice surpasses the Old Testament sacrifices such as burnt offerings and slaughter offerings mentioned in the main verse.
